items.title: Hinton Milt — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Hank Jones was the piano player, Barry Gells was the guitarist, O.C. Johnson drums and yours truly bass.

ctx.x: Yeah, her folks are from Mississippi, different places. Did you know Hank Jones is from Vicksburg, Mississippi?

items.title: Milt Hinton interviewed by Joe Williams, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995
items.q: That’s what we tried to do, the three of us, Hank Jones, Barry Galbraith, Osie Johnson and myself.

ctx.x: Yup, yup, yup. That was a beautiful time.

It was what you personified, and what you’ve always been like, I tell everybody and everybody says, “But Joe Williams can sing anything, I didn’t know nothing about a key.” They were playing what tune he wants, you know. And that’s what we tried to do, the three of us, Hank Jones, Barry Galbraith, Osie Johnson and myself. We tried to play for you what you, it’s your date, we’ve got to make you sound good. That’s what a rhythm section is supposed to do. If it’s my date then I’ll tell everybody what to do. On your…

It was beautiful to see the expression on your face and Osie’s and Hank, when the new music was put in front of you. I mean like, “Ayyy, yeah, hey look what we got,” you know. Wow, like it was like somebody bought you a new gift. Cause Jimmy Jones was writing then, and—

items.title: Jones Hank — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Milt Hinton was on that record. ... I think, it took a guy like Milt Hinton, Milt – – I don't know have you managed all the dates that he did because he took all the dates Bob Haggard used to have.

ctx.x: Now, you are going to Cleveland to do a concert, as opposed-­

Believe it or not, I did it. Some guy had written an arrangement as it was called "I Come to Demolish Cleveland." He had all sorts of funny noises and really weird sounds like laughing and stuff. Milt Hinton was on that record. That’s just an aside (laughs)
